message:
55M. My right hand has been numb and tingly for a few days, worse at night. No weakness anywhere, no face drooping, my speech is normal.

Additional patient information: It came on gradually over several days, not suddenly. There is still no weakness or trouble speaking.

output.reason: Subacute unilateral hand paresthesia without motor deficits or speech changes requires clinician evaluation to exclude structural or metabolic causes, but gradual onset and preserved strength and speech do not establish an emergency presentation.

output.reason: Gradual-onset right hand numbness and tingling over a few days, worse at night, with no reported weakness, facial droop or speech change — a pattern consistent with a common wrist nerve compression; no reported feature requires emergency, same-day in-person or clinician-dependent action now.
output.patientMessage: You can manage this at home for now. Numbness and tingling in one hand that builds gradually and is worse at night often comes from nerve pressure at the wrist, especially with the wrist bent during sleep; keeping the wrist straight at night and easing repeated wrist motions may help. If you develop sudden weakness, face droop or trouble speaking, call 911. If hand weakness, dropping things, loss of feeling, or numbness spreading up the arm or into the legs develops, message Counsel for clinician review, or be seen in person the same day if that review isn't available.
differential: Median nerve compression at the wrist (carpal tunnel syndrome)
Cervical radiculopathy or other nerve-root compression
Thoracic outlet or other brachial plexus compression

output.evidenceLimitations: Consumer health summaries describe typical carpal tunnel symptoms but do not confirm this diagnosis in this patient; the spinal cord compression syntheses are agent-compiled emergency-department references describing patterns (progressive weakness, sensory level, bowel/bladder change) that were not reported here. Symptom distribution beyond the hand, neck pain and bladder function are unreported and therefore unknown.
